High level asks: streaming responses for live transcripts, function/tool calling for their ticketing integration, and structured JSON outputs validated against a schema for downstream analytics.

- Provide a first-pass JSON schema for the two structured outputs they care about (invoice_summary, support_action).
- Outline streaming behavior (chunking/latency targets) and recommend retry/backoff for the tool-calls to their ticketing API.
- Surface any blocking security/compliance evidence they will request (we have their initial questionnaire).

Attachments: 2028-03-05_LaunchWell_SOW_v1.pdf

Launch timeline constraint: LaunchWell wants an internal pilot by end of Q2; they expect Sprint 0 to finish in two weeks.

Camila — you will own the onboarding plan and primary CS contact. Dylan — please supply the schema example + tool-call spec. Lauren — can you cover runbook/watchlist items for live output? Jasmine — please kick off the security questionnaire loop and map any needed artifacts.

Camila / Vanessa —

Appreciate the plan and timeline. A couple clarifications from our side before kickoff:
1) Schema requirements — we need two canonical outputs: 'invoice_summary' (for billing analytics) and 'support_action' (for ticket classification). The invoice_summary must include invoice_id, amount_cents, currency, line_items (array), and confidence_score. support_action should include ticket_id, action_type, suggested_assignee, and a list of extracted_entities. All fields should be strongly typed; nulls only for optional fields.
2) Tool-calls — our ticketing system (TicketPro) requires idempotency-key headers and 202 Accepted for async creates. Can you confirm Redwood's tool-call retry semantics if we get 202 vs 5xx?
3) Streaming — we prefer server-sent chunks every ~500ms for near-live UX; latency target <200ms per final chunk. If streaming backpressure is an issue we will accept batched 250–500 token chunks.

We can do the kickoff 3/09 at 10:00 PST. Attaching our implementation inbox (implementation@launchwell.com) and Priya (engineering lead) who will be on the call.

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Head of Product, LaunchWell

Samir — thanks for the specifics. Quick answers + an attached minimal schema (schema_example.json) you can iterate on.

Tool-call semantics
- For 202 Accepted (async) we surface a job_id and pollable status endpoint; recommended client behavior: poll with exponential backoff (start 500ms, cap 5s) until terminal state (succeeded/failed).
- For 5xx we retry with jittered backoff up to 3 attempts; for 4xx we surface the error to client. We support idempotency-key; include that header on create requests and we'll forward it to the downstream TicketPro adapter.

Streaming guidance
- Default chunk cadence: ~400–600ms for typical output when output rate permits.
- To hit <200ms perceived latency for the final chunk, we recommend enabling prefix caching + KV reuse on the session and keeping client window size >= 512 tokens.
- If LaunchWell wants deterministic chunk boundaries for their parser, enable the 'emit_json_records' flag which will ensure each chunk is a valid JSON record (newline-delimited).

Inline example (excerpt of schema_example.json):
{
  "$id": "https://redwood.ai/schemas/launchwell/invoice_summary.json",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["invoice_id", "amount_cents", "currency", "line_items"],
  "properties": {
    "invoice_id": {"type": "string"},
    "amount_cents": {"type": "integer"},
    "currency": {"type": "string"},
    "line_items": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object"}}
  }
}

I'll attach schema_example.json and a short validation script (Python) to the ticket after this thread. Also noting the security questionnaire — Jasmine, can you drop the SOC 2 artifact links into the shared drive for LaunchWell?

- Dylan
